narration: Financial gurus have told you for 30 years — skip your daily latte and retire rich. Here's why that advice is mathematically absurd.
visual: Coffee cup SVG with steam rising, large red X overlaid on cup, text 'THE LATTE LIE' at bottom, dark background with amber accent

narration: Do the real math. Your six-dollar coffee costs $2,190 a year. But the average American overspends on housing by $4,800 — more than double.
visual: Two horizontal bar charts on light background — amber bar growing to show coffee ($2,190/yr), then red bar growing larger showing housing overspend ($4,800/yr) with animated counters

narration: The 'big three' expenses are housing, car, and food. Most people obsess over coffee while their rent alone breaks the recommended 28% rule.
visual: House SVG center stage, two colored percentage bars below — green bar for 28% recommended, red bar for 32% actual — gap highlighted with $4,800 overspend badge, dark background

narration: Cars are the sneakiest drain. The average American spends $11,400 a year on transportation — five times the cost of their daily coffee.
visual: Blue car SVG animates in from left, then itemized cost breakdown appears: car payment $6,000 + gas/insurance $3,600 + maintenance $1,800 = $11,400 total counter, light background

narration: One smart housing decision saves more than five years of skipped coffees. You can't latte-boycott your way out of a structural spending problem.
visual: Coffee cup icon on left vs house icon on right, VS badge in center, callout box at bottom: '5 coffee-free years = 1 smart housing move', dark background

narration: Forget the latte guilt. Fix your housing, car, and grocery bill, and over 40 years that's over a million dollars more in your pocket.
visual: Three icons — house, car, grocery bag — each with green checkmark popping in sequence on light background, amber badge at bottom: '$1M+ SAVED over 40 years'
